title: Second Athenian League
capsule: The Second Athenian League (founded 378/377 BCE) was a maritime alliance of Aegean city-states organised to resist Spartan aggression following Sparta's illegal seizure of the Theban Cadmeia in 382 BCE. Its founding charter, preserved epigraphically (IG II² 43), explicitly prohibited Athenian cleruchies, tribute, and garrison imposition — protections designed to avoid the abuses of the Delian League — and governance was shared between Athens and a synedrion of allies. The league fractured in the Social War (357–355 BCE) when Rhodes, Chios, Kos, and Byzantium revolted successfully; Athens accepted their independence in 355, permanently ending the confederation's military significance.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Member states of the league are well documented epigraphically, but mapping actual territorial control is imprecise since membership conferred alliance rather than Athenian sovereignty over defined land areas.
